name: twisted-planter
why: The part the web playground opens first, so it has to build, and read right, on a stranger's first visit. Two bodies: a ruled star loft twisted 60° through nine sections, cut hollow by the same star inset 3 mm at the same section heights; seven drain holes; three Ø8 feet standing on 3·π·4² = 150.8 mm²; and a revolved saucer the feet touch and nothing else does. measure_wall_thickness reads the wall at 2.0 mm with the rim edge rounded; on the sharp rim it reports hundredths of a millimetre at the edge itself, where the flared facet meets the flat top at an acute angle, which is a ray leaving through the top face and not a thin wall. A 0.6 mm rim fillet built but cost a third of the build and 30k triangles in the browser, and a chamfer would not build on the twisted facets, so the rim is left sharp.
